text: The access-review requester is two activities on task queue `rwb-access` named `buildAccessReviewFile(reviewDate)` and `requestFileDelivery(manifest)`, called by the JOB-18 workflow of RWB-P4-AD008-APP. `buildAccessReviewFile` takes the review date, the starter identity and the feature switch, and returns the manifest plus the rwb-document document ID; the manifest carries the file name, the sha256, the record count, the business date, the interface ID, the requesting service `rwb-access` and the idempotency key `<interfaceId>:<businessDate>`. `requestFileDelivery` takes that manifest and returns the outbound item reference, the item status and the key, and stores the key in the `idempotency_key` object the platform library creates in `rwb_access`, so exactly one request exists per business date. The workflow, its workflow ID and the six-monthly Schedule stay with RWB-P4-AD008-APP, and the rwb-integration login name and the rwb-access login name are written as 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' until the platform DB story fixes them.
why: No source names a requester-side activity, its inputs and outputs, the manifest of a requesting service or the key format: Architecture v5 gives P2 the deliverFile activity and the manifest of four elements only, and the legacy story has no requester at all. Without a fixed shape the slice cannot be built, tested against the P2 fake or reviewed against a contract, and inventing a business value instead would be worse than fixing an assumption.

text: The access-review file is declared as one `interface_config` row of rwb-integration with direction OUTBOUND, and this story reads its interface ID, `file_pattern`, `data_product`, `owner_role` and `alert_role` at run time through the P2 contract and writes none of them in code; the extract layout and the recipient are declared with that row and with RWB-P4-AD008-APP. Every place where a literal interface ID, pattern, layout, recipient or alert target would otherwise appear carries the R9 placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B-P4-13-E1007-1; ASM-B-P4-13-E1007-2)', and no value is invented.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 names the JOB-18 job and its owner but no interface, no pattern, no layout and no recipient, and no FSD, TSD or legacy section supplies them. A requester cannot be wired to a file without those values, and the only safe form is to read them from the versioned interface row at run time and to mark the gap rather than to choose a business value.

text: The two delivery events are keyed by case ID and an access-review file carries no case, so this story does not read the event key: it matches an outcome to its own request by interfaceId, businessDate and fileId, dedupes in `processed_event` by consumer and CloudEvents id, and treats an outcome for an interface and business date it never requested as unmatched — recorded and routed to `.dlt` with an alert. No case key is read, no case route state is moved and no task is raised here; the owner task of a failed file is rwb-integration's and rwb-case's.
why: RWB-P2-E1007-CON fixes the key of both events as the case ID and its payload carries interfaceId and businessDate, while the access-review file has no case; without a stated matching rule a delivered outcome could not be tied to its request and a file-level failure could be lost or double-counted.

text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the capability area (CASE_RECORD or QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION), the right (C, R or U), the case reference, the case facts the caller presents (owner, queue, team, region), the field IDs whose masking is asked for and the request key, and answers the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the area, the right, the roles that carry the letter, the scope applied (OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL), the matrix version, the masking version, one masked or clear marker per field ID and the messageId of a refusal.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and the TSD appendix does not define it, so the request and the answer have to be fixed as a default before the story can be estimated or built; leaving them open would stop the slice.

text: The masking exceptions a role carries in the catalogue are the field IDs whose masking_rule row for that role at the masking version in force says unmasked true; every other field is an exception to nothing and is masked. text: The local decision-record table is created in rwb_access as decision_record with the entry fields of DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and the five columns the Work Package names, chain_seq bigint not null unique, prev_hash char(64) not null, entry_hash char(64) not null, corrects_entry_id uuid referencing decision_record (id) and actor_user_id uuid; the canonical form is the legacy BR4 rule (JSON with keys in alphabetical order, UTF-8, no spaces, timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC with microseconds, numbers as strings, empty fields as null) implemented once in CanonicalEntryForm; the genesis prev_hash is 64 zeros held as configuration; the chain lock is a PostgreSQL advisory lock on a per-service chain key; and the database login is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' until the platform DB story fixes it.
why: The Work Package fixes the five columns, the table name and the genesis value but no source publishes the rest of the column set, the canonical form for a per-service object, the lock key or the login, and the story cannot be built or tested on an empty definition.

text: The approved role file is the authority for the roster, the row counts and the file-carried labels of a role version. The story seeds exactly the rows the file holds, asserts the row counts of role, permission and role_conflict against the file and never against a constant, and reads the conflict version label from the file; the file must cover the role codes of TSD P4 T6.1.
why: No source states how many roles a role version holds, what the approved role file looks like, or which conflict version label it carries, so a count or a label written into the story would be an invented business value.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (role, permission, role_conflict) and T6.1 (the role list by capability column); FSD P4 v3 A2.3 and A2.4 (matrix versions PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12 with 756 permission rows); legacy RWB-E1-019 sections 3, 8 and 11
confirm: Security administrator (RW-SECADM) and reference data administrator (RW-REFADM): confirm the role-file layout, the roster and row counts of the version in force, and the conflict version label before the version is frozen.
impact: If the file holds rows the checks do not expect, the version is refused whole and nothing is written, so the impact is a delayed version rather than a wrong entitlement.

text: The effective date of a matrix version is held once per version, not once per row: role and permission carry no valid_from and no valid_to, so the read path resolves the version in force on a day as the latest approved version whose effective date is not later than that day. PM-2026.11 is effective 30 November 2026, the tentative release date, and PM-2026.12 is effective 1 December 2026 as the functional specification states.
why: TSD P4 T3.1 has no date column on role or permission, while FSD P4 A2.4 takes a matrix version into effect on a valid-from date; the story cannot invent a per-row column or ignore the effective date.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-044, no valid_from, no valid_to) and T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); FSD P4 v3 A2.1 and A2.4 (PM-2026.11 in the session, PM-2026.12 with validFrom 2026-12-01); R-UNI-38
confirm: Security administrator (RW-SECADM) and the rwb-access data model owner: confirm that a matrix version is dated once, and where that date is held, before the version is frozen.
impact: If the date is modelled per row later, the read predicate changes and the seeded rows gain a column; the version labels and the effective dates themselves do not change.

text: The conflict set is the set of pairs the approved role file names, and it must hold at least RW-SECADM with any business role (FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03) and RW-RISK with RW-REFADM (legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10). A pair that names an unknown role code or one role twice refuses the whole version, and the sign-in refusal is answered with the message ID MSG-P4-006 and the pair, with the message text carried as a placeholder because no source gives it.
why: No source holds the full list of conflicting role pairs or the text of MSG-P4-006; only two pairs and the message ID are named, so the story reads the list from the file and refuses anything it cannot resolve.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 (RW-SECADM with RW-CASEOWN, MSG-P4-006, incident to the security administrator queue, reason ROLE_CONFLICT) and AC-EXC-P4-004-02 (refused rows); legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10 (RW-RISK may not hold RW-REFADM) and BR9; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role_conflict
confirm: Security administrator (RW-SECADM): confirm the full conflict list and the approved wording of MSG-P4-006 before the version is frozen.
impact: A missing pair lets a person hold two roles that should not meet, which is the control CTL-08 finding the story exists to prevent; the checks fail closed on an unknown role code, so a wrong pair cannot be stored.
